findings.title: Authenticated WS session survives API-key rotation
findings.impact: stale session keeps receiving owner's private events indefinitely; owner-only filtering, no credential-generation check
findings.fix: session pins (owner, recovery_nonce) at auth; ws_auth_valid re-checks current recovery_nonce under a fresh short lock before every private event delivery and on non-auth frames; mismatch sends error frame and closes; old-key reconnect rejection preserved

findings.title: Permanent lockout on post-mutation snapshot failure (durability unknown wedge)
findings.impact: rotation applied in memory (old key dead, nonce burned) before durable ACK; any ACK failure / dropped request / lost response returned 503 unknown with no way to re-obtain the key; blind retry hits nonce mismatch
findings.fix: Account.recovery_last (in-memory only, serde-skip; snapshot/trailer format unchanged) records (nonce, new_key) per applied rotation; retry of the same signed authorization for the current generation returns the byte-identical key with zero mutation and still requires the durable ACK; superseded nonces still rejected; checked_add against u64 overflow

semantics.confirmed: rotation + durable ACK covering that recovery generation; key in response
semantics.unknown: rotation may be committed in memory; retrying the identical signed request is safe and idempotent (same key, no double nonce increment); no silent rollback or nonce reset
semantics.restart: forgets recovery_last; an un-ACKed generation's secret is never delivered after restart; client issues a fresh authorization (no permanent lockout)
